section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces the theory of ambivalence over emotional expression, defining it as an interactional deficit where individuals either inhibit expression or regret it. It highlights a theoretical gap regarding the boundary conditions of gratitude's beneficial effects, suggesting ambivalence over emotional expression as a potential moderator. The text reviews previous findings indicating that ambivalence over emotional expression negatively predicts life satisfaction and positive affect, and positively predicts depression and anxiety, demonstrating its link to lower well-being.
